source.title: A Two-Phase Perspective on Deep Learning Dynamics
source.citation: R. de Mello Koch et al., 2025
source.authors: R. de Mello Koch; Animik Ghosh

record.tranche_reason: The paper trains networks on small algorithmic datasets and tracks training and test accuracy over training steps, directly measuring grokking on its own models and settings.
record.gate_note: The paper also measures information-plane trajectories and test error. Its discussion of local complexity and the Linear Mapping Number, including detailed grokking dynamics attributed to cited work, is not a new measurement in this study.
record.test_reason: The authors train two-layer transformers on modular division (mod 96) and the S5 multiplication table and track train and test accuracy over steps. This is the original grokking measurement. They also track hidden-layer mutual information as a continuous progress measure.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors also argue the compression phase is not actively optimized by standard training and may be unnecessarily prolonged. They also draw a renormalization-group analogy, which is conceptual only.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses the same broad training-accuracy/test-accuracy-over-time approach to study algorithmic grokking, but reports experiments on division modulo 96 and S5 with a two-layer transformer, AdamW, and the stated training settings; the text does not give the original study's full recipe for direct comparison.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that the onset of the forgetting phase appears insensitive to layer depth in the two tested settings.

fits_no_version.finding: The onset of the information-plane forgetting phase is insensitive to layer depth (layer 1 vs layer 2) in both tasks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The compression-phase onset during grokking is uniform across network depth.

record.problems: Only two algorithmic datasets and fixed train-test splits are tested; training-set size is not varied. The paper reports no uncertainty estimates or controls. Several plotted values are not stated numerically in the text, and the S5 text does not establish that peak test accuracy is near-perfect.

untested.parts: Dependence of the delay on training-set size: only one fixed split per task (40-60, 50-50).
Formation of a specific generalizing circuit (e.g. Fourier) and removal of memorizing components. The circuit and LMN discussion relies only on cited work.
Weight decay is fixed at 0.0 and not varied. Grokking at zero weight decay is reported but is not a controlled test of V5.

record.verdict_notes: I dropped the reader's S5 limits_scope label. Unreported quantities (training-saturation time, final test accuracy) are cannot_determine, not evidence of a scope limit. The S5 caption does report well-separated phases, consistent with a delay. Grokking appears with weight decay 0.0, which is relevant context for V5 but not a test of it. Plots show steps only up to ~10^5–4×10^5, although training ran for 10^6 steps. No uncertainty is reported and each setting has a single run.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not vary training-set size, so it does not test whether delays grow as the training set shrinks.

It measures mutual-information trajectories and their timing relative to generalization, but does not measure formation of a specific circuit or Fourier algorithm, or removal of memorizing components.

rows.subject: two-transformer-layer model (modular division)
rows.operation_detail: Train on division modulo 96 and track test accuracy over steps
rows.value: Generalization occurs at ≈ 105 steps; test error vanishes later at around 105 steps
rows.note: The reported timing places generalization well after training error effectively vanishes.
rows.check: Exponents are garbled (10^5 written as 105). The text is also inconsistent. Sec 3.2 says the model starts to generalize midway between 10^3 and 10^4 steps and generalization ends around 10^5. The Fig 3 caption says generalization only occurs at ≈10^5. The value should record both statements.

rows.measure: Mutual-information trajectory, I(T;X) and I(T;Y), and its timing relative to generalization
rows.value: The text places the fitting-phase end midway between 103 and 104 steps and says generalization occurs around 105 steps; the information-plane trajectory's rightmost point coincides with the onset of the second descent
rows.note: The paper treats the information-plane trajectory as a progress measure; it does not identify a particular algorithmic circuit in this experiment.
rows.check: I(T;X) declines gradually after fitting ends and reaches a fixed point when test error vanishes. It is a continuous measure, not a circuit measure. Its turning point coincides with, rather than precedes, generalization onset. Exponents are garbled.

relationships.reason: Training error vanishes at ≈5×10^3 steps, but generalization completes only at ≈10^5 and test error then vanishes (R1–R3).
relationships.display_finding: Training error vanished around step 5,000, while generalization completed and test error vanished around step 100,000.

relationships.reason: After fitting, I(T;X) decreases gradually and reaches a fixed point when test error vanishes, so this continuous measure tracks the transition (R4, R8). No circuit is identified.
relationships.display_finding: After fitting, I(T;X) decreases gradually and reaches a fixed point when test error vanishes, tracking the transition without identifying a circuit.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: Training error effectively vanishes by ≈ 5 × 103 steps and generalization occurs around 105 steps; the text also reports vanishing test error (R1–R3).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports delayed generalization and a second descent, but does not state the training-accuracy saturation time or that peak test accuracy is near-perfect (R5–R7).

reader_labels.label: supports
